name: William R. Berkley Jr
current_role: President & CEO (and, since June 2026, Chairman) of W. R. Berkley Corporation
profile: W. Robert Berkley Jr. is the son of William R. Berkley, who founded commercial insurer W. R. Berkley Corp. in 1967 with $2,500 while studying for his Harvard MBA. The son joined the company in 1997, became President & CEO in 2015 (per Wikipedia), and was named chairman after his father died in June 2026.
interesting_fact: W. R. Berkley was founded in 1967 with $2,500 while the elder Berkley was an MBA student at Harvard; it grew into one of the largest US commercial lines insurers.
notes: IDENTITY: the Hurun $4.2B entry most likely reflects the founder William R. Berkley (not Jr.), who DIED in June 2026 aged 80 (source above). This record describes the living son W. Robert Berkley Jr. IR contact per company releases: Karen A. Horvath, VP External Financial Communications, (203) 629-3000 (corporate line); no published email found.

name: GM Rao
current_role: Founder Chairman, GMR Group (infrastructure: airports, energy, highways, urban development)
profile: Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao (b. 1950, Rajam, Andhra Pradesh) is a mechanical engineer who built GMR Group from a single jute mill bought in 1978 into one of India's largest infrastructure developers, running Delhi and Hyderabad airports plus energy and highway assets. He funded the move into power by selling his Vysya Bank stake; sons and family now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He used the roughly Rs 3.4 billion from selling his entire ING Vysya Bank stake to fund GMR's entry into power and infrastructure; the group is also co-owner of IPL cricket team Delhi Capitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked as a shift engineer at a paper mill and then as a junior engineer in the Andhra Pradesh Public Works Department; he moved into commodities trading at his mother's insistence.
notes: Press email reported from GMR's media page (page returned 503 when re-checked; verify). Philanthropy via GMR Varalakshmi Foundation (est. 1991). Strong energy/infrastructure fit for the podcast.

name: Daniel S. Loeb
current_role: Founder and CEO, Third Point LLC (hedge fund / activist investor, New York)
profile: Dan Loeb founded Third Point in 1995 with about $3 million and built it into a major activist hedge fund managing roughly $24 billion at end-2025, known for pointed letters to boards (Yahoo, Sony, Nestle, Disney). Recent positions include SK Hynix, Siemens Energy, Vistra and Microsoft, giving him an AI/power angle.
interesting_fact: Third Point's top Q4 2025 contributors included SK Hynix and Siemens Energy, with power producer Vistra among its holdings: a direct bet on the AI data-center and energy buildout.
deep_cut_fact: At age 12 he started a skateboard company, making boards for his friends; he is a lifelong surfer who grew up near the beach in Southern California.
notes: No published press email on Third Point's site; ir@ is investor-focused. Third Point's quarterly investor letters are public and a good conversation hook.

name: William Wrigley Jr
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Wrigley Management (Chicago single-family office) and WWJr. Enterprises (venture/PE vehicle)
profile: William "Beau" Wrigley Jr., great-grandson of the gum company's founder, ran Wm. Wrigley Jr. Co. from 1999, bought Altoids and Life Savers in 2005 and sold the firm to Mars for $23 billion in 2008. He later led cannabis firm Surterra/Parallel (2018 to ~2022) and now invests through his family office.
interesting_fact: His great-grandfather originally sold baking soda and switched to gum after noticing the gum he gave away as a premium was more popular than the product.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trustee of Conservation International, where he co-chairs its Ocean Health Council, and sits on the National Geographic Society's Council of Advisors.
notes: No published email or contact form found for Wrigley Management. Was an early chairman/investor in health-kiosk startup higi (MobiHealthNews 2016). Avoid Parallel lawsuits topic.

name: Chen Mingyong
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, OPPO (Guangdong Oppo Mobile Telecommunications)
profile: Chen Mingyong (Tony Chen, b. 1969, Wanyuan, Sichuan) studied at Zhejiang University, then followed Duan Yongping from Subor to BBK. He took over BBK's audio-visual business and the OPPO brand, launched OPPO's first phone in 2008, and built it into one of the world's top smartphone makers. He remains CEO and rarely gives interviews.
interesting_fact: He was one of six people who left Subor (Xiaobawang) with Duan Yongping in 1995 to start BBK, the group from which OPPO, vivo and OnePlus all descend.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Zhejiang University's information and electronic engineering department in 1992, he worked 1992-1995 at Zhongshan Subor (Xiaobawang) Electronics, the 'learning machine'/game-console maker, rising to assistant general manager.
notes: Very media-shy. press@oppo.com is the media contact in OPPO's Oct 2025 Find X9 global release (wire copy; could not re-load to verify). The SEC-insider tag 'UMC Vice President' in the input is likely a different person with the same romanized name; disregard.

name: Segolene Gallienne
current_role: Head of Champagne Lenoble (Damery) since 2023; director of Christian Dior SE, Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, Power Corporation of Canada and Château Cheval Blanc
profile: Ségolène Frère-Gallienne is the daughter of the late Albert Frère, Belgium's richest industrialist, and co-heir to the Frère holding with stakes in GBL (run by her husband Ian Gallienne). After PR roles at Belgacom/Proximus and five years leading communications at Dior Fine Jewelry, she sits on several boards and since 2023 runs the family's Lenoble Champagne house.
interesting_fact: She sits on the board of Château Cheval Blanc, the Saint-Émilion first growth co-owned by the Frère family and Bernard Arnault, and has been a director of Christian Dior SE since about 2010.
deep_cut_fact: She has a long-standing passion for gemology, and at Lenoble she has personally joined the grape harvest to understand the terroir; she redesigned the house's HQ with Dior Maison creative director Cordelia de Castellane as a free-to-visit family home.
notes: Contacts are for Champagne Lenoble (the business she runs), not personal. Private family; GBL press office is an alternative route. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes beyond GBL holdings.
